363	The Torah simply repeats itself from beginning to end.

364	In Parashat Terumah and Tetzaveh, the Torah commands

365	the Mishkan, two and a half parashot of Torah commanding

366	the Mishkan. This week the Torah tells one thing: they did

367	what they were commanded, one to one. The Torah goes through, compare:

368	Terumah, Tetzaveh: what they were commanded there, here they did. Everyone

369	who reads this wonders: why, why these 200 verses?

370	Every letter in the Torah is precise, every crown on

371	the letters is precise. After all, many of the disputes in

372	the Jewish people stem from the fact that the Torah

373	is brief in its wording. The Torah doesn't say tefillin. Each

374	of us buys tefillin for a thousand shekels, for 1,000

375	dollars. What does the Torah say about tefillin?

376	"And they shall be for totafot between your eyes." That is all

377	the Torah says: "You shall bind them as a sign on your hand, totafot

378	between your eyes." Not the color of the tefillin, not the shape of the

379	tefillin, not how to write them, not what to

380	write them on. The Torah is brief in its wording. All the laws of

381	shechitah, such difficult laws, "and you shall slaughter" — from this one phrase

382	the Sages learned, and passed down by tradition. The Torah doesn't speak

383	too much. The Torah is brief, the Torah is sparing with kinds,

384	sparing with words. Suddenly we arrive at Parashat Vayakhel-

385	Pekudei. The Torah speaks and speaks and speaks and speaks

386	about things that seemingly have no meaning, no

387	importance. They wouldn't have been written; everything would be the same if

388	these two parashot were missing. The Torah could have

389	written one verse: "Moshe gathered all the congregation of

390	the children of Israel and told them to build a Mishkan, and they did

391	as they were commanded," and we would understand that all is well.

392	Why does the Torah repeat, Parashat Vayakhel-Pekudei? So

393	we have said several times before a simple and

394	obvious principle: sometimes HaShem speaks about

395	something. When? When He loves it, when He loves

396	the subject. When something moving happens, then HaShem

397	speaks about it. And what happened in these parashot? People

398	gave money. What is more moving than people who overcome

399	their stinginess, overcome their ego,

400	and open their wallets? Moshe asked for money

401	for the Mishkan. Parashat Vayakhel describes a frenzy of giving

402	unmatched anywhere in the Torah. People ran: "And they brought

403	him still more freewill offering morning by morning." What is "morning

404	by morning"? Morning twice? The Kli Yakar says: first, they

405	didn't wait to be asked; they simply ran and gave

406	in the morning. Second, the Kli Yakar says something very beautiful.

407	He says: know that if you want to know whether a person

408	does something eagerly or reluctantly, you asked

409	a person for a loan. How do you know whether he

410	is waiting for you to hang up and manage on your own, or whether he

411	truly wants to give you? Look at his answer.

412	If he says, "Call me tomorrow morning,"

413	know that he is preparing the money; he is going to the bank tonight,

414	preparing the cash for you. If he

415	says, "Talk to me in the evening," know that he hopes

416	you will manage elsewhere. "And they brought him still more freewill offering morning

417	by morning." In the morning we do what we love; in the evening we do

418	what we have no choice about, what we can no longer put off.

419	The Torah says "morning" twice because they wanted to give.

420	They gave with such enthusiasm that, as the

421	parashah tells, they had to close the collection. How?

422	Moshe Rabbeinu said: "The people are bringing too much." Vayakhel: stop

423	bringing money. It is the only fundraiser in history

424	that ended with people coming and saying, "Don't bring any more." There is no

425	money in the bank, the bank said there is no more money, don't bring

426	more, there is no room to put it. People gave and poured out freewill offerings,

427	such giving as there never was in history. So

433	about it, and repeats it, and repeats it. Let us read:

469	something harder: giving time. Many people

471	your hands and your feet, to give time and devote
